evidence: sql_runner.py:73 calls psycopg2.extensions.parse_dsn(connection_string) with no try/except, so a malformed DSN raises psycopg2.ProgrammingError at construction. psycopg2 source was not read and not run here, so its accept/return behavior is unverified. The claim's 'DSN strings SQL Lens accepts' is undefined: I did not find a validator that restricts DSNs, and no stated requirement is shown broken by the unguarded raise.

sql_runner.py:122 calls psycopg2.connect(self.connection_string, **self._connection_options), where options only hold connect_timeout (lines 74-79). psycopg2.connect(dsn=None, ..., **kwargs) merges via make_dsn(dsn, **kwargs): kwargs are appended to the DSN parameters, and on a duplicate key the kwarg overrides rather than raising. So passing a DSN plus keywords is supported and supplements it. Based on my knowledge of psycopg2 semantics; the psycopg2 source was not in the view.

sql_runner.py:70-79 (head): in the connection_string branch only kwargs['connect_timeout'] is copied into _connection_options; line 122 connects with psycopg2.connect(self.connection_string, **self._connection_options), so other kwargs such as sslmode are silently dropped. The docstring at line 57 says '**kwargs: Additional psycopg2 connection parameters (sslmode, connect_timeout, etc.)'. Input: PostgresRunner(connection_string=dsn, sslmode='require') connects without sslmode. The host/database branch (line 88) does forward kwargs. The base also dropped all kwargs in the DSN branch (base lines 107, 109), so this is not new, but the authored docstring is still wrong for the DSN branch.

sql_runner.py:78 and :90 use `not os.environ.get("PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT")`. Empty string is falsy so the 5s default is applied. But whitespace-only (e.g. " ") is truthy, so it is NOT treated as unset and no default is applied; the claim's whitespace part is wrong. On libpq: getenv returns non-NULL for an empty value so libpq takes it as the set value, and as I recall an empty connect_timeout parses to 0 (no timeout). That would differ from the 5s default applied here, so the 'must match libpq' part is doubtful too. I did not run libpq or read its source in this environment, so that part rests on recall.

sql_runner.py:78,90 check os.environ PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT only at construction, to decide whether to inject a default connect_timeout. But when the env var is set at construction, no connect_timeout is stored (lines 78, 90), and run_sql (lines 122/124) calls psycopg2.connect, where libpq reads PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT at each connect. So later env changes do affect later connections (e.g. unset later gives no timeout; changed value takes effect). Conversely, if unset at construction, the injected default of _DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides a later-set env var. The claim is only true for the injection decision, not for connection behaviour.

tests/unit/test_sql_runner_cleanup.py:131-134 stubs psycopg2.extensions.parse_dsn as lambda _dsn: {} and registers it in sys.modules. Real parse_dsn returns a dict; the test DSN 'postgresql://u:p@h/d' has no connect_timeout, so {} is what the real function would give for that key check. Stub matches what the runner needs.

sql_runner.py:60-64 imports psycopg2 and stores the module as self.psycopg2; run_sql calls self.psycopg2.connect at lines 122 and 124. The test patches the connect attribute on the same module object (test line 34), and attribute lookup at call time hits the mock. The asserted call_args therefore come from the real code path.

run_sql (sql_runner.py:121-174): connect returns the MagicMock; set_session(readonly=True) is a MagicMock call (default read_only=True); statement_timeout_ms=0 skips the setup cursor; is_read_shaped('SELECT 1 AS n') is true (readonly.py:52-60, first-keyword check), so it takes the named-cursor path with cursor_factory. conn.cursor(...) returns connection.cursor.return_value, whose fetchmany returns [{'n': 1}]. cap is 10000 (no effective settings bound), so rows_to_capped_df (limits.py:57-72) builds pd.DataFrame([{'n':1}]) with column 'n' and truncated False. cursor.close and conn.close are mocks. The test asserts result['n'].tolist()==[1].

pyproject.toml:106-107 [tool.pytest.ini_options] sets asyncio_mode = "auto"; pytest-asyncio>=0.23 is a dependency (line 60). Test file defines async tests at lines 24 and 44 with no asyncio marker, so auto mode collects and awaits them.

psycopg2 parse_dsn wraps libpq PQconninfoParse, which unquotes single-quoted values, so connect_timeout='0' yields {'connect_timeout': '0'} and int() gives 0. sql_runner.py:73-79 applies the default only when 'connect_timeout' is absent from the parsed DSN params, so the key's presence suppresses the default. The test at tests/unit/test_postgres_connect_timeout.py:18,39-40 matches. I did not run the test.

preflight.py:34 _DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5 (used at lines 99,131); postgres sql_runner.py:17 default is 5. Precedence at sql_runner.py:75-79: DSN connect_timeout (any value incl. 0, via parse_dsn key presence) leaves options empty; else kwargs connect_timeout; else if PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT unset, 5; if the env var is set, nothing is supplied so libpq uses it. Hostless-params path (90-91) is consistent. Adversarial input: DSN with connect_timeout=0 is preserved because only key presence is checked.

tests/unit/test_postgres_connect_timeout.py:13-23 parametrizes URI DSN (line 14), keyword DSN (15), individual params (16, 19), and combined cases. Both tests monkeypatch psycopg2.connect with a MagicMock (lines 34, 52) before run_sql, so no network connection is opened. Hostnames are example.invalid. If psycopg2 is not installed the tests skip via importorskip, which also opens no connection.

factory.py:216 passes the normalized URL (query string kept) as connection_string to PostgresRunner. sql_runner.py:73-79: parse_dsn; if connect_timeout is in the DSN (including 0) no option is added, so the DSN wins. Otherwise the constructor kwarg is used, else the 5s default is added unless PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is set, in which case libpq reads the env var. Line 122 passes the default explicitly to connect, and explicit parameters override service-file values in libpq. Hostile input tried: connect_timeout=0 in the URL. It is in dsn_params, so no default is injected and 0 is preserved. The host/database/user path (lines 90-91) behaves the same way.

sql_runner.py:70-91: DSN path sets connect_timeout=5 only if absent from DSN (parse_dsn), absent from kwargs, and PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT unset/empty; params path (80-91) likewise. run_sql (121-124) passes these on every connect. Other connections (preflight.py:99) use their own explicit timeout; factory.py:216 builds PostgresRunner. Hostile input: DSN with connect_timeout, or env set; both correctly skip default.
